newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Thirteen killed in attacks in Kinshasa -minister.
newsitem.headline: Thirteen killed in attacks in Kinshasa -minister.

text.p: At least 13 people died in a wave of attacks in a single night in the capital of Democratic Republic of the Congo, a government minister said on Monday.
Interior Minister Mwenze Kongolo described Sunday night's attacks as the work of "criminals trying to sabotage the government" of President Laurent Kabila.

"It concerns a dozen killed, precisely 13 people killed," Mwenze said on state television. "Investigations are continuing to apprehend the bandits. They are criminals trying to sabotage the government."
Residents said dead bodies with bullet wounds lay in the streets of Kinshasa'a working class districts of Bandalungwa, Kasa-Vubu, Ngiri-Ngiri and Kimbanseke.
"Many Kinshasa residents woke up this morning to find out that streets were strewn with dead bodies. Several people were shot dead last night," state radio said.
The minister called on residents of the city of more than five million people to remain calm.
The television said five of the attackers had been arrested.
The crime rate in Kinshasa has soared since Kabila overthrew veteran president Mobutu Sese Seko in May after a seven-month guerrilla campaign.
Thieves and house-breakers caught red-handed have been lynched or burned to death. The interim governor of Kinshasa has vowed to punish anyone resorting to "private justice."
It was not immediately clear whether those killed on Sunday night were suspected criminals or robbery victims.
But an official statement read out on radio on Monday said the killings were not the work of Kabila's Alliance forces.
"A group of armed criminals claiming to be members of the Alliance forces are committing many crimes. The police will finally track them down," it said.
